def factor_range_reversal_directional_filter(df):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    range_ = df_copy["high"] - df_copy["low"]
    close = df_copy["close"]
    ret_5d = close / close.shift(5) - 1
    range_mean = range_.rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    range_std = range_.rolling(20, min_periods=20).std(ddof=1)
    range_z = (range_ - range_mean) / range_std.replace(0, np.nan)
    raw_reversal = -ret_5d * range_z
    ret = close.pct_change()
    lookback = 20
    up_sum = ret.clip(lower=0).rolling(lookback, min_periods=lookback).sum()
    down_sum = (-ret.clip(upper=0)).rolling(lookback, min_periods=lookback).sum()
    total_abs = up_sum + down_sum
    direction_ratio = up_sum / total_abs.replace(0, np.nan)
    direction_ratio = direction_ratio.clip(0, 1).fillna(0.5)
    regime_weight = 1.0 - direction_ratio
    raw = raw_reversal * regime_weight
    factor = raw.ewm(span=3, adjust=False).mean()
    df_copy["factor_range_reversal_directional_filter"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_range_reversal_directional_filter"]
description: Crossover combining the elite range-expansion reversal mechanism from parent 1 (sharp drops with elevated range suggest oversold bounce) with a directional consistency filter adapted from parent 2. The base signal captures mean-reversion potential when volatility spikes. The added regime weight dampens the reversal signal when the recent 20-day up-day ratio is high (strong persistent trend), and amplifies it when directional consistency is low (choppy, mean-reverting conditions). This lightweight modulation improves signal reliability across market regimes, targeting higher ICIR and MI while preserving the parent's strong RankICIR.
